# Nissaraṇiya Sutta (Iti 72 (It 3.23 PTS It 61))

**ID:** Iti 72 (It 3.23 PTS It 61)
**Section:** Itivuttaka (iti)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-2
**Title (Pali):** Nissaraṇiya Sutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Elements of Escape
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/iti72

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Nissaraṇiya Sutta* ("Elements of Escape") is the 72nd discourse of the *Itivuttaka*, located in the third section (It 3.23, PTS p. 61) [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. Delivered with the traditional *Itivuttaka* framing, the discourse expounds three properties or elements of escape (*tisso nissaraṇiyā dhātuyo*): renunciation (*nekkhamma*) as the escape from sensuality (*kāma*); the formless (*āruppa*) as the escape from forms (*rūpa*); and cessation (*nirodha*) as the escape from whatever is produced, conditioned, and dependently arisen (*bhūtaṁ saṅkhataṁ paṭiccasamuppannaṁ*) [SuttaCentral; Windisch 1889]. The teaching concludes with verses declaring that a monk who thoroughly comprehends the escape from forms and the stilling of all conditioned things (*sabbasaṅkhārasamatha*) attains liberation and arrives at peace through higher knowledge (*abhiññāvosito*) [Windisch 1889].

In his 1889 editio princeps for the Pali Text Society, Ernst Windisch documented manuscript corruption in the verse section of the discourse, noting that certain Burmese and Sinhalese manuscripts erroneously interpolated a segment from the following discourse (Iti 73) [Windisch 1889]. The sutta has received numerous modern renderings, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates that Iti 72 shares phraseology across 87 matching passages with 17 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Within the *Itivuttaka*, it exhibits notable textual overlap with Iti 85 (*Asubhānupassī Sutta*), Iti 53 (*Dutiyavedanā Sutta*), and Iti 51 (*Dhātu Sutta*) [DharmaNexus]. Outside the *Itivuttaka*, substantial shared phrasing is found in the *Tikanipāta* (AN 3), *Dasakanipāta* (AN 10), *Magga Saṁyutta* (SN 45), and the *Paṭisambhidāmagga* (Ps 1.1 and Ps 3.10) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-canonical alignments, DharmaNexus detects matches with the Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (T 99, fascicle 17) [DharmaNexus].
